author: haiku
label: climb-05-01
changes: Did not run the junior loop, because no junior questions or answers were supplied; this is the step 6 rewrite from the brief and the plan alone, and the teach-back has not been run.

Restructured into the required order: a summary paragraph, then how the system works today, then terms, then numbered steps, then a failure table, then the open questions. Build and rollout work is split into its own section, separate from how the system runs.

Moved the row query module and the email templates into a 'Shared parts' section, because several steps depend on them. This removed the old cross-references to step numbers (for example 'step 4 of this list' and 'step 11').

Merged the old steps 3 and 11 into shared parts. Merged the old steps 4, 5 and 6 into the click path, and moved the old steps 1, 2, 12 and 13 into 'Building and rolling out'. The old 13 steps became 5 path steps plus the build list.

Changed the job's step list from a run of letters into labelled items a to i, and each item now says what it does in full. Step 4, item b, now says to send the ready email, instead of pointing at another step.
Removed the phrase 'or after a retry-stopping failure, per the queue's rules'. The queue documentation only says the final failure handler runs once after the last attempt fails.

Added a plain sentence of reason where a part appears (why two paths, why keyset paging, why the file is only visible at completion, why an access failure returns normally instead of retrying, why the stale limits exist).
Added terms that the plan used without defining: primary database, read replica, keyset paging, multipart upload, attempt, heartbeat, stale, expired, export row. Each is defined in one plain line.

Kept every fixed value, the exports table and its single-writer rule, the storage behaviour, the API endpoints and their error codes, the page states, and the eight open questions. Did not change what the plan does.
Added a single failure table covering the cross-cutting cases, so a reader can see all failure handling in one place. Each step still says what happens when it goes wrong.

Cut the duplicated wording from the summary, the fixed values, and the Storage/Access/Rebuild test lines. Merged the 'Done, expired' page state into the page-states list. Kept the test list complete, but tied each check to the step that owns it.
Kept the 'Not in this plan' section unchanged.
